verdict.summary: Calendly OAuth app creation and production setup are documented as self-service for anyone with a Calendly account, with no stated app-review submission or certification fee. Plan around implementing PKCE S256, a single immutable redirect URI per app, minimum scopes, and separate Sandbox and Production registrations.
verdict.activeEffort: The active work is standard OAuth integration work: create separate Sandbox and Production apps, securely retain the one-time-displayed credentials, implement PKCE S256, and request only endpoint-required scopes.
verdict.waitTime: No provider approval wait is described in the reviewed production workflow; it says to create a Production app when ready for real customer data.
verdict.mainGate: The main technical gate is a valid OAuth authorization request with the app's registered redirect URI, PKCE S256, and scopes that cover the endpoints used.

steps.title: Sign in to Calendly and create a Sandbox OAuth app

detail.text: A Calendly account is required; in the Developer Portal's OAuth apps tab, create an app and select Sandbox for development and testing.

sources.quote: Log in to Calendly, or sign up for a Calendly account.
On the OAuth apps tab, select Create OAuth app .
Environment type : select Sandbox for development and testing, or Production when your app is ready for real users.

steps.title: Choose the Sandbox callback URL and scopes before saving

detail.text: Each app accepts exactly one redirect URI, and setup requires at least one scope. Sandbox permits HTTPS URIs and HTTP only on localhost.

sources.quote: Redirect URI : the URL where Calendly sends users after they authorize your app. Enter exactly one URI.
Select the scopes that your app needs. Select at least one scope.
Sandbox https URIs, and http URIs on localhost . Example: http://localhost:1234/callback

detail.text: Calendly displays a client ID, client secret, and webhook signing key after registration; the client secret and webhook signing key cannot be viewed again.

sources.quote: Copy all three values and store them securely before you leave this screen. You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again.

detail.text: Map every planned API endpoint to its required scope and request the minimum set. Write scopes implicitly include their corresponding read scopes.

sources.quote: When your app initiates an OAuth flow, it should request the minimum set of scopes needed for your use cases.
A :write scope implicitly includes the corresponding :read scope within the same domain.
Overly broad scopes can lead to unnecessary user friction at install time.

steps.title: Implement OAuth authorization-code flow with PKCE

detail.text: Implement PKCE using S256, send the registered redirect URI, validate the callback, and securely exchange and store tokens once credentials are available.

sources.quote: Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the S256 method.
If the authorization request does not include a code challenge, the request fails.
The redirect URI for your OAuth application

detail.text: Throttle token requests to eight per connected user per minute and design API retries around per-user limits of 500 requests per minute on paid plans or 50 on free plans.

sources.quote: Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within a span of 1 minute.
Paid Plans 500 requests per user per minute
Free Plan 50 requests per user per minute
Rate limits are enforced per user.

steps.title: Run Sandbox authorization and endpoint tests

detail.text: Test successful authorization, declined permissions, token exchange, and each endpoint under the exact requested scope set; confirm that the user granted all requested scopes.

sources.quote: Confirm that the user granted all requested scopes (users can decline scopes during install).
When a request is missing required scopes, the API returns an error indicating insufficient permissions.

steps.title: Verify the authorization endpoint is reachable

sources.quote: HTTP 301 -> https://calendly.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=probe-not-a-real-client&response_type=code&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexa (mentions "client_id")

steps.title: Create a separate Production OAuth app

detail.text: Create a second app for real customer data, select Production, and register the final HTTPS callback URL; Production permits HTTPS redirect URIs only.

sources.quote: Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.
Production https URIs only

detail.text: If the production app later needs additional scopes, initiate reauthorization for existing installs and verify the resulting grants before calling newly scoped endpoints.

sources.quote: For existing installs, you may need to reauthorize the app to request additional scopes.
Verify that the scopes requested during installation include all required by the endpoint you are calling.

gotchas.text: A redirect URI is not a list: each OAuth app accepts exactly one URI, so use separate Sandbox and Production apps and plan callback changes carefully.

sources.quote: Redirect URI : the URL where Calendly sends users after they authorize your app. Enter exactly one URI.
We recommend that you start with a Sandbox app for development. Create a second app for Production when you are ready to use real customer data.

gotchas.text: PKCE with S256 is mandatory; an authorization request without a code challenge fails.

sources.quote: Every OAuth app must use Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) with the S256 method.
If the authorization request does not include a code challenge, the request fails.

gotchas.text: Save the client secret and webhook signing key immediately because they cannot be displayed again.

sources.quote: Copy all three values and store them securely before you leave this screen. You cannot view the client secret or the webhook signing key again.

gotchas.text: New OAuth apps have no API access until scopes are explicitly requested and user-approved, and users can decline requested scopes.

sources.quote: For newly created OAuth apps and new Personal Access Tokens, no API access is granted until scopes are explicitly requested and approved.
Confirm that the user granted all requested scopes (users can decline scopes during install).

gotchas.text: OAuth token requests are limited to eight per user per minute, independently of the general per-user API limit.

sources.quote: Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within a span of 1 minute.
Rate limits are enforced per user.

whenBlocked.text: For insufficient-permission errors, verify that the scopes requested during installation cover the endpoint and have the user reauthorize if scopes were added after installation.

sources.quote: When a request is missing required scopes, the API returns an error indicating insufficient permissions.
Verify that the scopes requested during installation include all required by the endpoint you are calling.
For existing installs, you may need to reauthorize the app to request additional scopes.

whenBlocked.text: For authorization failures, ensure the request uses the app's redirect URI and includes an S256 PKCE code challenge.

sources.quote: The redirect URI for your OAuth application
Every OAuth app must use PKCE conforming to RFC 7636, with the S256 method.

whenBlocked.text: If connections or token refreshes are failing under load, queue and back off token requests to remain below eight token requests per user per minute.

sources.quote: Only 8 OAuth tokens per user can be requested within a span of 1 minute.

uncertain: The reviewed official pages do not state a Sandbox test-user cap or connected-account cap.
The reviewed official pages do not state a formal Production review timeline, certification submission, or app-review fee.
The reviewed evidence does not state whether a redirect URI can be edited after an app is created.
